examples.text: As for shooting a man from behind a wall, it is cruelly like to stalking a deer.

glosses: A particular episode of trying to follow or contact someone.

examples.text: With manly mien he stalked along the ground.

glosses: To move slowly with the abdomen close to the ground.

examples.text: Lizards and snakes crept over the ground.
One evening, while the Rabbit was lying there alone, watching the ants that ran to and fro between his velvet paws in the grass, he saw two strange beings creep out of the tall bracken near him.

shivering in the autumn wind

has not yet come

pocked with narrow caves

glosses: To grow across a surface rather than upwards.
To move slowly and quietly in a particular direction.

examples.text: He tried to creep past the guard without being seen.
Electrification of the Eastern Region main line from Strasbourg, incidentally, is steadily creeping nearer to Paris, and is now complete as far as Château Thierry, 59 miles away; [...].

glosses: To make small gradual changes, usually in a particular direction.

examples.text: Prices have been creeping up all year.

glosses: To move in a stealthy or secret manner; to move imperceptibly or clandestinely; to steal in; to insinuate itself or oneself.

examples.text: Old age creeps upon us.
[…]guard his understanding from being imposed on by the willful or at least undesigned sophistry which creeps into most of the books of argument.

glosses: To slip, or to become slightly displaced.

examples.text: The collodion on a negative, or a coat of varnish, may creep in drying.

glosses: To move or behave with servility or exaggerated humility; to fawn.

examples.text: A creeping sycophant.

glosses: To have a sensation as of insects creeping on the skin of the body; to crawl.

examples.text: The sight made my flesh creep.

glosses: To drag in deep water with creepers, as for recovering a submarine cable.

glosses: The movement of something that creeps (like worms or snails).
A relatively small gradual change, variation or deviation (from a planned value) in a measure.
